briefs.findings: Owner-approved vision: one reader saves articles and marks them read without losing title or address. Accounts, sharing and recommendations excluded. Design fixes local Node, JSON persistence, queue-owned state and presentation via public operations. Glossary agrees; no material contradictions.
limitations: No instructions, standards, audit or requirements beyond these three documents.

briefs.findings: Documented boundary: queue owns article state; presentation uses save/list/mark-read and cannot write storage directly. No implementation, entry points or tests exist. No runtime behaviour inferred.
limitations: No executable architecture to assess. History has two documentation commits; measurements are advisory.

briefs.findings: No manifests, lockfiles, native config, check scripts or CI exist. Inspect and inventory pass. Host Node v24.17.0 and Git 2.54.0 are available; these are host versions, not project pins.
limitations: No project check or user journey can execute.

briefs.findings: Approved Node stack can use the built-in node:test runner through node --test for behaviour checks. Official filesystem documentation warns against overlapping writes without awaiting completion; serialize JSON mutations if asynchronous persistence is used.
limitations: No JS versus TS choice or project version is imposed; no existing tool conventions to extend.

briefs.findings: No third-party integration is documented or implemented; no outside service research or live probe is relevant.
